header_sentences: See Mount of Olives; and see Oil, and Olive-tree.

contexts.text: A leaf of an olive... () = a little of the truth of faith... An olive = the good of charity.
That an olive = the good of charity, is evident not only from the signification of an olive, but also of oil, in the Word. Illustrated.

The two olives () = the Celestial and the Spiritual; thus the love which is of the Celestial Church, and the charity which is of the Spiritual Church. These are at the Lord's right and left hands. AC 4197:4.
Some species of trees = interior goods and truths, which are of the spiritual man; as olives and vines.
Oil of olive = spiritual good.
To tread the olive, but not to anoint () = to be instructed concerning the good of life, but still not to live in it.
Olive () = celestial love. AC 10261:3, Illustrated.
Berries of olives () = the holy goods in the Celestial Kingdom: their truths are signified by sons of olives.
These are the two olives, and the two candlesticks... () = love and intelligence, or charity and faith...
The reason an olive = love and charity, is that an olive tree = the Celestial Church; and therefore an olive, which is its fruit, = celestial love, which love is love to the Lord... Illustrated.
But the goods of love to the Lord are meant in the Word by the fruits of trees, especially by olives.
[155a] 4. The dove stood on a branch from which grew an olive.
The fruits of truth are signified in the Word by grapes; the fruits of good, by olives.
The honour of an olive () = celestial good.
The olive, as the fruit from which comes oil, corresponds to the good of love in act.
The work of the olive shall lie () = that there is no celestial good.
That such things are signified by olive groves, olive trees, and olives, in the Word. Illustrated.
That olive tree, and olive = the good of love. Illustrated.
These which are born from this spiritual affection are compared to olive plants () because through truths are produced the goods of love and of charity, which are olives.
By a leaf is signified truth, and by an olive () the good born thence.
